force.title: The Compute Super-Cycle
force.signature: AI's hunger for power is reshaping the grid and everything plugged into it — whoever has electricity, land, and cooling near the data centers wins a once-in-a-generation buildout.

A \u00b7 Where the machines live: AI compute demand turns land, power, and cooling into the scarce inputs of the decade.
Connectivity and hosting ride the same demand surge underneath the AI boom.
The software that runs on top
Enterprise and data software monetize the compute build-out.
B \u00b7 The power scramble: Data centers need firm power now; gas, solar, wind, and hydro all get pulled in.
Transmission and gas delivery — not generation — become the real constraint.
C \u00b7 The physical trades of the buil: Electricians, cooling contractors, and turbine makers are the picks-and-shovels of compute.
Data centers are also a construction-materials story — concrete, steel, and heavy build.
D \u00b7 The tensions: Whoever can't get power — homes, factories, small ISPs — pays more or waits.
Cooling water and waste heat turn into constraints and opportunities.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: AI made electricity and land scarce again; the power-and-buildout chain is the trade of the decade.
